recent_posts.title: Beyond SQL Generation: How to Teach Agents What Your Database Means
recent_posts.summary: AI models can generate syntactically correct SQL but often fail to return meaningful results because they lack business context. Kris Jenkins, Lead Developer Advocate at Snowflake, presents a solution using semantic models and the OSI (Open Semantic Interface) standard. These tools provide AI agents with a structured understanding of what database tables represent, how entities relate, and what business rules apply — bridging the gap between SQL syntax knowledge and domain-aware query generation. The talk covers how to implement semantic models declaratively, why the OSI standard matters, and how to build a reliable AI-powered database analyst.

recent_posts.title: “We Don’t Store Your Data” Isn’t Enough: How Regolo.ai’s Zero Data Retention Policy Actually Works
recent_posts.summary: When building AI-powered applications in regulated industries, the common claim 'we don't train on your data' is insufficient. Zero data retention (ZDR) means no prompt or response content is written to persistent storage after inference completes — a stronger guarantee than simply opting out of model training. GDPR Article 5(1)(e) and the EU AI Act increasingly require this level of control. Regolo.ai, built by Italian cloud company Seeweb, implements ZDR as an architectural property: requests flow through to GPU inference, responses are returned, and nothing is persisted beyond minimal billing metadata. Conversation state becomes the developer's responsibility. A real-world example is Aegis by Euraika, a compliance management platform that uses Regolo.ai to handle sensitive regulatory data without creating data governance problems. The platform offers standard API compatibility, open-weight models, EU data residency, and pay-as-you-go or flat monthly pricing with a 30-day free trial.

recent_posts.title: Astro vs Next.js: Two Philosophies for Building the Modern Web
recent_posts.summary: A detailed comparison of Astro and Next.js framed around a fundamental question: are you building a content site or a web application? Astro's zero-JavaScript-by-default philosophy and Islands Architecture make it ideal for blogs, documentation, and marketing pages where performance is paramount. Next.js, with React Server Components, ISR, API routes, and Server Actions, is better suited for SaaS products, dashboards, and e-commerce requiring rich interactivity and integrated backend logic. The piece walks through concrete code examples for both frameworks covering data fetching, hydration control, and developer experience, and notes that the two frameworks are converging — both moving toward less client-side JavaScript — but remain distinct tools for distinct use cases.

recent_posts.title: Java virtual threads vs Kotlin coroutines in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A preview of a Codemotion Madrid 2026 talk by JetBrains' Wout Werkman comparing Java's Virtual Threads (Project Loom, introduced in Java 21) with Kotlin's coroutines. The piece covers the history of Java's concurrency limitations, how Kotlin coroutines addressed them, and how Java responded with Virtual Threads, Scoped Values, and Structured Concurrency APIs. The central question is whether Java has finally closed the gap with Kotlin's long-standing concurrency model.

recent_posts.title: Snowflake – “Beyond SQL Generation”: Teaching AI Agents What Your Database Really Means
recent_posts.summary: AI agents can write syntactically correct SQL but fail in production because they lack domain knowledge about what database columns, tables, and business logic actually mean. The solution is a semantic model — a structured file encoding tacit domain knowledge such as table relationships, column meanings, deprecated fields, and valid query patterns. This approach, to be demonstrated by Kris Jenkins (Lead Developer Advocate at Snowflake) at Codemotion Rome 2026, aims to build reliable AI database analysts from day one rather than through months of prompt engineering and fixes.

recent_posts.title: AI literacy in 2026 means governing agents not just using them
recent_posts.summary: AI literacy in 2026 goes beyond using AI tools — it requires governing them. The post outlines five pillars: technical foundations (AI, ML, deep learning), generative AI and prompting techniques (few-shot, chain-of-thought), agentic AI systems that act autonomously, prompt engineering and fine-tuning, and data quality with ethical guardrails. It introduces a maturity framework — Consumer, Practitioner, Governor — arguing that teams at the Governor level, who understand training, agentic deployment, and data strategy, are the ones defining their industries. Practical starting points include auditing team literacy, automating one repetitive workflow with human checkpoints, and prioritizing data quality over model quality.

recent_posts.title: What an AI prediction failure at Sanremo teaches us about predictive models
recent_posts.summary: An experiment using Google's Gemini AI to predict the winner of the 2026 Sanremo music festival reveals the fundamental limitations of AI predictive systems. Gemini produced a detailed, data-driven analysis drawing on streaming stats, jury votes, bookmaker odds, and historical patterns, confidently naming Serena Brancale as the winner. She finished ninth. The actual winner, Sal Da Vinci, had been predicted third due to an assumed press jury bias that never materialized. The post-mortem identifies three core failure modes: over-reliance on bookmaker odds, conflating streaming popularity with televoting mobilization, and inability to account for unquantifiable live moments like an emotional on-stage performance going viral. The broader lesson is that AI models excel at pattern recognition in historical data but cannot see variables they were never given — making them tools for reducing uncertainty, not eliminating it. Anyone selling AI as an oracle is doing marketing, not science.

recent_posts.title: MiniMax M2.5 offers frontier coding performance at a fraction of Western AI prices
recent_posts.summary: MiniMax M2.5, launched February 12, 2026, is a 230B parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 10B parameters per query, achieving near-parity with Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5 on coding benchmarks like SWE-Bench Verified (80.2%) at roughly 1/20th the output cost ($1.20 vs $25 per million tokens). The Lightning variant runs at 100 tokens/second for $0.30 input/$2.40 output per million tokens. MiniMax completed a $619M Hong Kong IPO with shares doubling on day one to a ~$13B market cap. The model features an 'architect mindset' trained across 200,000+ real environments, supports 10+ programming languages, and handles 204,800-token context windows. Full weights are open-sourced on Hugging Face under a modified MIT license. The piece contextualizes M2.5 within the broader pattern of Chinese AI labs turning US chip embargo constraints into efficiency-driven innovation advantages, while raising questions about data sovereignty, long-term financial sustainability, and regulatory fit under the EU AI Act.

recent_posts.title: The Engineering of the Possible: Beyond the “Best Practices” Dogma
recent_posts.summary: A pragmatic critique of dogmatic adherence to software engineering 'best practices' like Clean Code, TDD, microservices, and Agile. The author argues that canonical advice from industry gurus assumes ideal greenfield conditions that rarely exist in practice. Real seniority means knowing when to break the rules: managing technical debt consciously, resisting unnecessary complexity (e.g., microservices for 100 users), accepting compliance constraints, and delivering working solutions within real constraints rather than chasing theoretical perfection.

recent_posts.title: The Year of Maturity: AI in 2026 Between Autonomous Agents, Sovereignty, and the Reinvention of Work
recent_posts.summary: Drawing on 2026 outlooks from Info-Tech, NTT DATA, and Deloitte, this analysis argues that AI has crossed from experimentation into an operational phase. Key themes include: the 'proof-of-concept trap' giving way to a flywheel effect for leaders who embed AI into core infrastructure; the rise of agentic AI systems that act autonomously across enterprise workflows; the emergence of sovereign AI as a geopolitical and regulatory reality forcing hybrid, regionally partitioned architectures; the workforce tension between 'vibe coding' democratization and expert-first amplification strategies; AI's expansion into physical systems like cobots and drones; and governance becoming a prerequisite for scale rather than a compliance burden. The decisive competitive variable in 2026 is no longer model capability but data infrastructure resilience, governance maturity, and organizational redesign for human–AI collaboration.

top_posts.title: How ChatGPT Can Help Developers Transition from Junior to Senior Roles
top_posts.summary: ChatGPT and similar AI tools can significantly aid developers by analyzing code, suggesting improvements, writing tests, and more. Their effectiveness depends on clear, specific prompts. While they are not designed to solve new or niche problems independently, they excel in tasks like code contextualization, reviews, and documentation. Tools like GitHub Copilot leverage additional context to provide more relevant suggestions, bridging the gap between junior and senior developer roles.

top_posts.title: Creating a Fallout-Style UI Using Modern CSS
top_posts.summary: Learn how to create a retro-futuristic user interface inspired by the Pip-Boy 3000 from the Fallout series using modern CSS techniques. The tutorial covers semantic HTML, responsiveness, typography and colors, responsive layout, visual effects and animations, and using generative AI for sci-fi content.

top_posts.title: How to Know You’ve Become a Senior Programmer
top_posts.summary: Senior programmers face increasing complexity and responsibility as they strive to ensure code maintainability and quality. Over time, they shift from making rapid changes to carefully evaluating the impacts of their actions, often incorporating extensive testing and documentation. This evolution from impulsive coding to cautious development reflects a deeper understanding of the potential repercussions changes can have on a system, highlighting the importance of risk assessment and thorough planning in software development.

top_posts.title: “A Programmer Who Reads Is Worth Two”: Tech Books for Summer 2025
top_posts.summary: A curated list of 14 technical books for summer 2025 reading, covering diverse topics from building LLMs from scratch and AI agents to cybersecurity, Kubernetes, quantum computing, and documentation. The selection includes both hands-on technical guides and broader philosophical works on AI's impact on society, catering to developers looking to expand their knowledge across multiple domains.
